==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=SystemJson&min=SystemJson&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/SystemJsonTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=SystemJson&min=SystemJson&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Text.Json;

// Verify.SystemJson: Writes System.Text.Json types, JsonDocument, JsonElement and the JsonNode family, as readable snapshots.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.SystemJson
// Note: The default snapshot is Verify's relaxed json in a .verified.txt, which is deliberate: it
// is easier to read than strict json.
// Note: UseStrictJson() switches to a .verified.json. Applied globally it changes every snapshot
// in the assembly, so a project wanting both forms needs two test assemblies.
// Note: Json values that map to a known guid format are scrubbed with no opt-in.
// Note: VerifierSettings.ScrubInlineDateTimes and VerifierSettings.ScrubInlineGuids are the
// assembly-wide forms of the inline scrubbers.
// Note: This covers the System.Text.Json type family only; JObject and JArray need
// Verify.NewtonsoftJson.
public class SystemJsonTests
{
    // Without this extension a JsonDocument serializes as its internal structure. With it the
    // snapshot is the json itself, in Verify's relaxed form: a .verified.txt, not a .verified.json.
    // Values that parse as a guid are scrubbed on the way, so an id generated per run is stable.
    [Fact]
    public Task ParseJsonDocument()
    {
        var json =
            """
            {
              "short": {
                "original": "http://www.foo.com/",
                "short": "foo",
                "error": {
                  "code": 0,
                  "msg": "No action taken"
                }
              }
            }
            """;

        var document = JsonDocument.Parse(json);
        return Verify(document);
    }
}
